٧٥٦٤ — عن رجل من وفد عبد القيس، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( لا تشربوا في نقير ولا مزفت ولا دباء، ولا حنتم، واشربوا في الجلد الموكى عليه، فإن اشتد فاكسروه بالماء، فإن أعياكم فأهريقوه )).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٩٥)، والبيهقي (٨/٣٠٢).
7564 — A man from the delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Do not drink from hollowed palm trunks, pitch-coated vessels, gourds, or green jars. Drink from leather that is tied closed. If it becomes strong, weaken it with water. If it overcomes you, pour it away.”
 Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3695) and al-Bayhaqi (8/302).

٧٥٦٦ — عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه قال لوفد عبد القيس: (( لا تشربوا في نقير، ولا مقير، ولا دباء، ولا حنتم، ولا مزادة، ولكن اشربوا في سقاء أحدكم غير مسكر، فإن خشي شرته فليصب عليه الماء )).
 حسن: رواه البيهقي (٨/٣٠٢).
والحاصل من هذه الأحاديث أنه يجوز شرب النبيذ ما دام حلواً، أما إذا أقام يومين أو نحوها ولم يجد فيه رائحة أو تغيراً فلا تشرب تورعاً، وافعل كما فعل النبي ﷺ إنه سقاه خادمه أو أمر بإهراقه.

7566 — Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said to the delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays: “Do not drink from hollowed palm trunks, pitch-coated vessels, gourds, green jars, or large water skins whose tops have been cut off. Rather, drink from one of your leather water skins, without intoxication. If one fears its strength, let him pour water over it.”
 Hasan: Narrated by al-Bayhaqi (8/302).
The conclusion from these hadiths is that it is permissible to drink infusion as long as it remains sweet. But if it remains for two days or around that and no smell or change is found in it, then do not drink it out of caution. Do as the Prophet ﷺ did: he either gave it to his servant to drink or ordered it to be poured away.

٧٥٦٧ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه قال: نهى النبي ﷺ عن الزبيب والتمر، والبسر والرطب.
 وفي رواية: نهى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ عن التمر والزبيب، ونهى عن التمر والبُسر أن يُنبذا جميعاً.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٦٠١)، ومسلم (١٩٨٦:١٨). والرواية الأخرى للنسائي (٥٥٦٠).

7567 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade mixing raisins with dates, and unripe dates with fresh dates.
 In another narration: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade dates and raisins, and he forbade dates and unripe dates from being made into infusion together.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5601) and Muslim (1986:18). The other narration is from al-Nasa’i (5560).

 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٦٠٢)، ومسلم (١٩٨٨:٢٤). واللفظ للبخاري.

7580 — Abu al-Waddak said: I will not drink infusion after hearing Abu Sa‘id say: A drunken man was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “I did not drink wine; I only drank raisins and dates in a gourd.” He said: He ordered that he be pushed with hands and struck with sandals. He forbade gourds, and he forbade raisins and dates, meaning that they be mixed together.

 Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1983). Abu Dawud (3675) narrated it through another route with the wording: Abu Talhah asked the Prophet ﷺ about orphans who had inherited wine. He said: “Pour it away.” He said: “Shall I not make it into vinegar?” He said: “No.”

7584 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Wine is cursed in ten ways: itself, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who consumes its price, the one who drinks it, and the one who serves it.”
 Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3674), Ibn Majah (3380), Ahmad (4787), Ibn Abi Shaybah (6/447), and al-Bayhaqi (5/327).

٧٥٨٦ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عباس قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( أتاني جبريل فقال: يا محمد إن اللّٰه عز وجل قد لعن الخمر، وعاصرها، ومعتصرها، وشاربها، وحاملها، والمحمولة إليه، وبائعها، ومبتاعها، وساقيها، ومستقيها )).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٨٩٧)، والبيهقي في الشعب (٥١٩٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥٣٥٦)، والحاكم (٤/١٤٥).
7586 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Gabriel came to me and said: ‘O Muhammad, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who drinks it, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, the one who serves it, and the one who asks to be served it.’”
 Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (2897), al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu‘ab (5196), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (5356) and al-Hakim (4/145).
